text: The patient presents with acute chest pain radiating to the left arm. ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. Troponin levels are elevated at 2.5 ng/mL. Blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg.
Routine follow-up visit. Patient reports feeling well with no new complaints. Vitals within normal limits. Blood work unremarkable. Continue current medications.
Patient admitted with severe shortness of breath and bilateral crackles on auscultation. Chest X-ray reveals bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. SpO2 88% on room air. Started on supplemental oxygen.
Annual physical examination. Patient is a 45-year-old male in good health. BMI 24.5. Cholesterol and glucose levels normal. No family history of cardiac disease.
Emergency presentation with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and slurred speech. CT head shows no hemorrhage. NIHSS score 8. Within thrombolysis window.
Patient presents for medication refill. Hypertension well controlled on current regimen. Home BP readings average 128/78. No side effects reported.
Severe abdominal pain with guarding and rebound tenderness in right lower quadrant. WBC 15,000. CT abdomen shows inflamed appendix with possible perforation.
Wellness visit. Patient exercises regularly, follows Mediterranean diet. All screening tests up to date. No concerns raised during visit.
Patient brought in by ambulance after witnessed seizure lasting 5 minutes. Post-ictal confusion. No prior seizure history. Glucose normal. Head CT pending.
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes. HbA1c improved from 7.8% to 6.9%. Patient compliant with metformin and lifestyle modifications. Continue current plan.
Acute presentation with high fever 39.8°C, productive cough with purulent sputum, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. CXR shows right lower lobe consolidation.
Routine dermatology check. No suspicious lesions identified. Patient counseled on sun protection. Return in 12 months.
Patient presents with sudden severe headache described as worst of life. Neck stiffness present. CT head negative. Lumbar puncture shows xanthochromia.
Well-child visit for 8-year-old. Growth and development appropriate for age. Immunizations up to date. Vision and hearing screening normal.
Elderly patient found unresponsive at home. GCS 7. Right pupil dilated and fixed. CT shows large right-sided subdural hematoma with midline shift.
Patient reports occasional mild knee pain after prolonged walking. Physical exam unremarkable. Range of motion full. Advised weight management and quad strengthening.
Chest pain with new onset atrial fibrillation. Heart rate 150 bpm. BP 100/70. Troponin mildly elevated. Echo shows moderate LV dysfunction EF 35%.
Routine eye examination. Visual acuity 20/20 bilateral. Intraocular pressures normal. No diabetic retinopathy. Return in one year.
Acute confusion in nursing home resident. New-onset fever, dysuria, and suprapubic tenderness. Urine dipstick positive for nitrites and leukocytes. WBC 18,000.
Sports physical for 16-year-old athlete. No cardiac symptoms. Family history negative for sudden cardiac death. Physical exam normal. Cleared for sport participation.
Patient with known cirrhosis presents with hematemesis and melena. HR 120, BP 85/50. Hemoglobin 6.2 g/dL. Large-bore IV access established. Blood products ordered.
Prenatal visit at 28 weeks. Fetal growth appropriate. Glucose tolerance test normal. Blood pressure 110/70. No proteinuria. Patient feeling well.
Severe allergic reaction with facial angioedema, urticaria, and stridor after bee sting. Epinephrine administered. Monitoring for biphasic reaction.
Routine colonoscopy screening. No polyps identified. Cecum reached and landmarks identified. Next screening in 10 years.
Acute myocardial infarction STEMI anterior wall. Emergent cardiac catheterization shows complete LAD occlusion. PCI with stent deployment performed.
Patient seen for annual flu vaccination. No contraindications identified. Vaccine administered. Patient tolerated well. No immediate adverse reactions.
Diabetic ketoacidosis with blood glucose 580 mg/dL, pH 7.15, bicarbonate 8. Anion gap 28. Insulin drip and aggressive IV fluids initiated.
Routine blood donation screening. Hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL. Vital signs normal. No recent illness or travel. Eligible for donation.
Status epilepticus not responding to initial benzodiazepine therapy. Second-line antiepileptic loading initiated. Intubation may be required if seizures continue.
Patient presents for routine mammogram. No palpable masses. Family history of breast cancer in maternal aunt at age 65. Screening performed.
Massive pulmonary embolism with right heart strain on CT. Troponin elevated. Hemodynamically unstable. tPA thrombolysis initiated.
Dental cleaning and examination. No cavities detected. Mild gingivitis noted. Flossing instruction provided. Return in 6 months.
Necrotizing fasciitis of right lower extremity. Crepitus on palpation. WBC 22,000. Lactate 6.5. Emergent surgical debridement required.
Routine physical therapy follow-up for chronic low back pain. Patient reports 50% improvement with exercises. Continue home program.
Ruptured ectopic pregnancy with hemoperitoneum. Patient is tachycardic and hypotensive. Emergency laparoscopy scheduled. Two units pRBCs transfusing.
Well-woman exam. Pap smear performed. Breast exam normal. Patient counseled on contraception options. Follow up for pap results.
Decompensated heart failure NYHA class IV. BNP 3500. Severe peripheral edema. Requiring IV diuretics and inotropic support in ICU.
Routine vaccination visit for 2-month-old infant. Growth parameters at 50th percentile. Developmental milestones appropriate. Vaccines administered per schedule.
Acute pancreatitis with lipase 1500 U/L. Severe epigastric pain radiating to back. CT shows peripancreatic inflammation. NPO status and IV fluids.
Insurance physical examination. 35-year-old female in excellent health. All vitals normal. Labs within reference ranges. Cleared for coverage.
Septic shock from urosepsis. MAP 55 despite 3L fluid resuscitation. Norepinephrine started. Blood and urine cultures obtained. Broad spectrum antibiotics given.
Follow-up visit for seasonal allergies. Symptoms well controlled on cetirizine. No need for medication change. Return PRN.
Acute meningitis presentation. Fever 40.1°C, photophobia, nuchal rigidity, petechial rash. CSF shows 2000 WBCs, predominantly neutrophils. IV ceftriaxone stat.
Routine optometry visit. Mild presbyopia. New reading glasses prescribed. No pathology identified on dilated exam.
Massive upper GI hemorrhage. Patient vomiting large volumes of fresh blood. HR 140 BP 70/40. Hemoglobin 5.1. Massive transfusion protocol activated.
Annual wellness physical. 50-year-old male. PSA 1.2. Lipid panel normal. Blood pressure 124/76. Healthy lifestyle. No interventions needed.
Tension pneumothorax. Absent breath sounds on left. Tracheal deviation to right. Hypotensive. Needle decompression performed followed by chest tube insertion.
Patient seen for travel medicine consultation. Planning trip to Southeast Asia. Appropriate vaccinations and malaria prophylaxis prescribed.
Unstable angina with dynamic ST changes. Positive troponin trend. TIMI score 5. Heparin drip initiated. Urgent cardiology consult for catheterization.
Routine hearing test for occupational health screening. Audiometry within normal limits bilaterally. No workplace hearing protection changes needed.
Acute aortic dissection Type A. Severe tearing chest pain radiating to back. CT angiogram confirms dissection from aortic root. Emergent cardiac surgery consulted.
Well-baby check at 6 months. Weight gain appropriate. Sitting independently. Babbling. No parental concerns. Solid foods introduction discussed.
Hypertensive emergency with BP 240/140. New-onset confusion and bilateral papilledema. Serum creatinine elevated at 3.2. IV nicardipine drip initiated.
Annual gynecologic examination. Normal findings. HPV co-testing performed. Contraception counseled. No abnormalities noted on bimanual exam.
Complete heart block with ventricular rate 32 bpm. Patient symptomatic with near-syncope. Transcutaneous pacing initiated. Cardiology for emergent pacemaker.
Routine podiatry visit for diabetic foot care. No ulcers or deformities. Sensation intact bilaterally. Nails trimmed. Appropriate footwear confirmed.
Fulminant hepatic failure with INR 4.8 ammonia 180 and grade III hepatic encephalopathy. Transplant evaluation initiated urgently.
Pre-employment physical. 28-year-old in good health. Drug screening negative. Hearing and vision normal. Cleared for employment.
Acute limb ischemia right lower extremity. 6Ps present: pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis, poikilothermia. Vascular surgery emergent consult.
Routine pediatric check-up for 4-year-old. Developmental screening normal. BMI at 55th percentile. Vision screening passed. School readiness discussed.
Cardiogenic shock post-MI. EF 15% on bedside echo. Requiring vasopressors and IABP support. Multidisciplinary team conference for management.
Patient returns for suture removal 10 days post minor laceration repair. Wound well healed without signs of infection. Sutures removed.
Anaphylactic shock after IV contrast administration. Airway edema respiratory distress BP 60/30. Second dose epinephrine given. Crash cart at bedside.
Nutritional counseling visit. Patient seeking guidance on plant-based diet. BMI 22. Labs normal. Discussed B12 supplementation and protein sources.
Acute stroke with large vessel occlusion MCA territory. ASPECTS 7. Within thrombectomy window. Neurointerventional team activated for mechanical thrombectomy.
Routine lab review visit. Thyroid function normal. Complete blood count within limits. Comprehensive metabolic panel unremarkable. Continue current management.
Traumatic brain injury GCS 5 after motor vehicle collision. Bilateral fixed dilated pupils. Large epidural hematoma on CT. Neurosurgery emergent evacuation.
Annual diabetic eye screening. No background retinopathy. Visual acuity stable. Pressures normal. Continue glucose optimization. Return annually.
Massive saddle pulmonary embolism. RV failure on echo. Cardiac arrest in ED. ROSC after 8 minutes CPR. tPA administered during resuscitation.
Healthy adolescent sport physical. No murmur no marfan features. Family history negative for sudden death. ECG normal. Full clearance given.
Acute mesenteric ischemia. Severe abdominal pain out of proportion to exam. Lactate 8.2 metabolic acidosis. CT angio shows SMA occlusion. Emergent OR.
Routine dental X-rays and examination. No new caries. Existing restorations intact. Periodontal measurements stable. Continue regular hygiene visits.
Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm. Patient complaining of severe back pain syncope episode. BP 70/50 HR 130. CT confirms 8cm AAA with retroperitoneal hemorrhage.
Weight management consultation. BMI 27 patient motivated to lose weight. Discussed caloric deficit exercise plan meal planning. Follow up in one month.
Acute respiratory distress syndrome ARDS. P/F ratio 85. Bilateral diffuse infiltrates. Ventilator settings optimized for lung-protective strategy. Prone positioning initiated.
Patient presents for contact lens fitting. Refraction stable from last visit. Trial lenses dispensed. Return in one week for follow-up assessment.
Thyroid storm with fever 40.5C HR 170 altered mental status. TSH undetectable free T4 markedly elevated. PTU methimazole beta-blockade and hydrocortisone initiated.
Annual comprehensive physical 60-year-old female. Bone density normal. Mammogram scheduled. Colonoscopy current. All labs within normal limits.
Acute compartment syndrome right forearm after fracture. Severe pain with passive extension. Compartment pressures 45 mmHg. Emergent fasciotomy required.
Routine childhood immunization visit. 12-month-old receiving MMR and varicella vaccines. Growth normal. No contraindications. Vaccines administered.
Eclampsia at 34 weeks gestation. Tonic-clonic seizure witnessed. BP 190/120. Magnesium sulfate loading dose given. Emergent cesarean section planned.
Annual health screening for 40-year-old executive. Stress test normal. Echocardiogram normal. Hormonal panel normal. Lifestyle counseling provided.
Acute epidural hematoma with uncal herniation signs. Fixed dilated right pupil. GCS declining from 13 to 7 over 30 minutes. Emergent craniotomy indicated.
Pre-surgical clearance for elective knee arthroscopy. Cardiac risk assessment low. Labs normal. ECG normal sinus rhythm. Cleared for surgery.
Toxic megacolon in ulcerative colitis. Abdominal distension colon diameter 8cm on X-ray. Fever tachycardia. Failed medical management. Surgical colectomy planned.
Well-woman annual exam 30-year-old. Breast exam normal. Pap smear collected. Contraception reviewed. Prenatal vitamins discussed for future planning.
Cardiac tamponade. Beck's triad present: hypotension, JVD, muffled heart sounds. Pulsus paradoxus 20 mmHg. Emergent pericardiocentesis performed with echo guidance.
Routine blood pressure check. Home readings consistently 120/75. Weight stable. Current antihypertensive regimen effective. Continue same plan.
Acute adrenal crisis. Hypotension refractory to fluids. Hyponatremia hyperkalemia. Known Addison's disease. IV hydrocortisone 100mg stat and q8h.
Six-month dental cleaning. No new issues. Mild tartar buildup removed. Oral hygiene satisfactory. Next appointment in 6 months.
Fat embolism syndrome post long bone fracture. Petechial rash, acute hypoxia, altered mental status. Supportive care with mechanical ventilation in ICU.
Routine vision screening at school health fair. 20/20 bilateral. Color vision normal. No referral needed. Certificate of normal vision provided.
Malignant hyperthermia during general anesthesia. Temperature rising rapidly to 41C. Muscle rigidity. Dantrolene administered immediately. Surgery aborted. ICU transfer.
Follow-up appointment for mild eczema. Condition improved with topical emollient. Continue moisturizing routine. Return only if worsening.
Acute liver failure from acetaminophen overdose. INR 6.2, ammonia 250, grade IV encephalopathy. NAC infusion running. Urgent transplant listing evaluation.
Routine physical therapy discharge. Patient met all functional goals. Independent with home exercise program. No further PT sessions needed.
